children: , the enterprise-computing and hybrid-cloud giant, launched an open-source Lunar Foundation Model with NASA. The stock climbed approximately 2% to $238.62 Friday.

Built from more than 30 data layers gathered by nine instruments across four NASA missions, the model can flag potential ice deposits, chart craters for safer landings and examine volcanic terrain. Benchmark testing showed accuracy gains of as much as 23% over commonly used techniques, giving IBM a powerful showcase for applying AI to complex scientific data.

The picture adds a useful valuation signal: IBM trades 1.64% below its GF Value estimate of $242.59, suggesting modest upside rather than a deep discount. Open sourcing the lunar model will not generate meaningful licensing revenue by itself. The bigger prize is proving that IBM can turn enormous datasets into specialized AI systemsand then sell the computing infrastructure, software and consulting expertise needed to deploy them on Earth.

title: IBM Gains 2% as Lunar AI Beats Mapping Methods by 23%
